import pandas as pd

# Load source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source3_9_0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_9/training_0.csv"
source3_9_1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_9/training_1.csv"

source3_9_0 = pd.read_csv(source3_9_0_path, index_col=0)
source3_9_1 = pd.read_csv(source3_9_1_path, index_col=0)

# Operation 1: JOIN Source3_9_0 and Source3_9_1 on "scientific_name"
joined_df = pd.merge(source3_9_0, source3_9_1, on="scientific_name", how="inner")

# Operation 2: group_by Source3_9_1.park_name and aggregate count of Source3_9_1.observations
# Note: The aggregation is count of observations, so count number of rows per park_name
# Since observations column is numeric, but the operation is count, we count non-null observations per park_name

# Group by park_name from Source3_9_1 (which is now in joined_df)
grouped = joined_df.groupby("park_name")["observations"].count().reset_index()

# Rename columns to match target schema
grouped.rename(columns={"park_name": "park_name", "observations": "observations"}, inplace=True)

# Ensure data types match target schema: park_name as string, observations as integer
grouped["park_name"] = grouped["park_name"].astype(str)
grouped["observations"] = grouped["observations"].astype(int)

# Write the result to the target path
target_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_9/target_multisource.csv"
grouped.to_csv(target_path, index=False)
